chapter: Glen Gray band: Red Nichols and Bobby Hackett
title: Red Nichols asks to join the Glen Gray band
summary: Challis, who did the hiring of 4-F wartime musicians, doubted Nichols's temperament but O'Keefe overruled him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: And Nichols. We lived up -- up at the end of the drive there at the time I was with Whiteman, and Nichols was doing the show with Don Voorhees, Don Voorhees or Roger Kahn. I think he had written a show then. But anyway, let me see now.

See, well, the three of us were well acquainted with each other. So O'Keefe comes to me one day as the manager, and he was also one of the members of the corporation, and by this time the corporation had -- had been pretty much dissolved, and he and Glen Gray owned the band as a partnership.

Now, he came to me one time because, you know, we had to dig around for 4-F -- through 4-Fs, and this was my job. You know, I go from one band -- what band had he played with? What -- where did this guy come from that I was supposed to hire. And he would either -- he would tell me all the time, I've been with Benny Goodman; I was with this band and that

band.'"

So I would have to dig around, see who he was, and usually I found out so many guys we got in the band, and you'd have to let them go, because they were either dopes or -- some reason why they're 4-Fs. Some of them we had were excellent.

Anyway, we were always looking for trumpet players. So he came to me one day, and he said, "Nichols is coming up. He'd like to join the band. What do you think?" Frankly, I was against it. I thought, "We got enough headaches," and here's Nichols coming in the band --

-- out of the war plant or -- I didn't worry about his playing because I know he's -- he's an expert. You know, he knows what to do with something. He's great in the studio, and he was great recording. But it's just a matter of he was also a fantastic angler, you know. Miff -- I think he could have given Miff a better deal, Miff Mol and his Moilers. And there was always Red and Miff together. They made all those records. But Red's the guy that came out on top.

Anyway, I told him that. But then he overruled me. He said, "Well, the first thing I know, we're going out to Chicago, and there's Red. So, you know, so I said, "If this is the way it is, this is the way it is.""
